key_reasoning.reason: New GitTarget delivery abstraction (targets/git-target.ts) plus a new prompt-free GitRunner (targets/git-client.ts), with coordinated changes to settings types, config-store validation, install/install-command, status, uninstall (working-copy removal), run-sync dispatch, marker, redact, the analytics CLI index and the shared src/utils/errors.ts (SyncGitError/GitFailureCause). Base L: many components, but all inside the one analytics-sync subsystem. The red flag for integration with a new external service (a team git remote) bumps it to XL.

No prior git-target precedent. The closest pattern is webhook-target.ts, which covers neither git argument-injection guards (every positional after '--' or behind a fixed prefix), userinfo-credential redaction in git URLs, path-escape guarding of the slug folder, nor unattended prompt-free git (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, ssh BatchMode, no hooks or signing). That security gap bumps M to L. Shallow-clone refresh/re-clone logic, a non-fast-forward rebase retry loop and stderr classification add to the novelty. The security red flag (credential redaction, injection-surface hardening, visible in the 'harden git sync target after code review' commit) then bumps it to XL.

The diffstat reports 26 files changed (3040 insertions, 215 deletions), across src/cli/commands/analytics/, src/utils/, tests/integration/ and docs/. New files: targets/git-target.ts, targets/git-client.ts, install-command.ts and their tests plus the integration test. The 16+ band makes this XXL.

Four layers change. CLI/API: the analytics sync install/status/uninstall flags. Service: run-sync dispatch and the GitTarget logic. Persistence: the analytics-sync.json GitSettings schema, a separate git last-sent marker and the on-disk working copy. External: the git remote over the network. Base L; the new-external-integration red flag bumps it to XL.

The implemented contract is coherent: git-repo/branch/path flags, slug-folder isolation, no force-push and no stored token. A follow-up hardening commit after code review shows that edge cases (security and branch handling) were refined late, which scores M. This matches the local L calibration example profile-provider-decoupling (RC=M).

Total 26 sits on the L/XL boundary (26 to 27), and Technical Risk and Component Scope are both at XL, so the borderline rule would lean higher. The score is kept at L because the work is one subsystem in one repo, adds no new packages, and is less spread out than the nearest project anchor, profile-provider-decoupling (L, 23, 6 areas across 4+ subsystems). The bundled XL anchor epmcdme-10303 (27) reached XL only through heavyweight new dependencies (Dependencies=XL); this change has none. Scores are not inflated to force a split (G1).
